title: History 13: Seeing in 3D: NeRF, Gaussian splats and structured latents

questions.q: What does NeRF's network take and return?
options: A 5D coordinate in, and a density and a view-dependent colour out
A photo in, and a mesh out
A prompt in, and a splat out
A voxel grid in, and a depth map out
questions.answer: A 5D coordinate in, and a density and a view-dependent colour out
questions.why: The abstract says so. The picture comes from adding those answers along each ray.

questions.q: Why is splatting so much faster to draw than NeRF?
options: It projects stored blobs with no network query for each point along each ray
questions.answer: It projects stored blobs with no network query for each point along each ray
questions.why: At 192 samples a ray, an 800 x 800 NeRF image is about 123 million queries. A splat renderer needs no network at draw time.

questions.q: Why do the same three blobs give a different picture when unsorted?
options: Blending depends on which is in front, since each blocks what's behind it
questions.answer: Blending depends on which is in front, since each blocks what's behind it
questions.why: The lab gives [0.25, 0.5, 0.125] sorted, and [0.5, 0.25, 0.125] in stored order.

questions.q: Does Chroma Radiance's NerfEmbedder make it a 3D model?
options: No: it adds a 2D positional encoding to image patches
questions.answer: No: it adds a 2D positional encoding to image patches
questions.why: The class docstring says 2D positional encoding. The name is borrowed from the coordinate-network idea.

questions.q: A wall 0.04 thick is seen with 16 samples over a length of 4. What does the lab show?
options: Opacity 0: the samples step over it
questions.answer: Opacity 0: the samples step over it
questions.why: Spacing is 0.25, far wider than the wall. Only finer sampling or sampling near surfaces finds it.
